s: here; in this place; refers to an environment one is currently in, or to something within reach
Ich bin hier in diesem Dorf geboren.
I was born here in this village.
Setzen wir uns hier aufs Sofa.
Let’s sit down here on the sofa.
there; right there; in that place; refers to something that is considered nearby, or can be seen and pointed at
Die Kirche ist gleich hier am Ende der Straße.
The church is right there at the end of the street.
Siehst du die Wolke hier neben der Bergspitze?
Can you see that cloud there next to the mountain top?
Die Frist wurde hier überhaupt nicht erwähnt.
The deadline was not mentioned here at all.
used with the definite article or the determiner dieser (“this, that”) to express proximity (“this”)
Die Kneipe hier ist sehr beliebt.
hier.et:
From Middle High German hier, from Old High German hier, from Proto-West Germanic *hēr. Cognate with Dutch hier, English here, Swedish här.
The predominant form in Middle High German and throughout modern dialects of High German is hie (and variants) with loss…

s: listen, hey; Used for emphasis or to call for attention, often when broaching a new subject, but not as a greeting
Hier, der Markus ist doch jetzt auch verheiratet, ne?
Hey, wait, Markus is married now, too, isn't he?
"Hier, ich wollte mal fragen: Ist im Dezember wirklich die Wolle alle? Und wird die Seife gestreckt?"
"Hey, so I wanted to ask: Are we really going to run out of wool in December? And is the soap being stretched?"
hier.et:
From Middle High German hier, from Old High German hier, from Proto-West Germanic *hēr. Cognate with Dutch hier, English here, Swedish här.
The predominant form in Middle High German and throughout modern dialects of High German is hie (and variants) with loss…

Hieb.et: 15th century, derived from hieb (Middle High German hiew etc.), the older preterite of hauen.

s: to here, here (to this place), hither
to heave (lift and move something with great difficulty)
Er hievte sich aus dem Bett.
He heaved himself out of the bed.
Die Müllmänner hieven den Müll in den Müllwagen.
The garbage collectors put the garbage into the garbage truck.
to heave (pull up with a rope)
Lange Wachen gibt es: der Streek dauert drei bis vier Stunden; saure Arbeit, denn die Zungen sitzen mehr im Schlick als im Sand und die Kurre ist oft nicht zu hieven.

s: Ich erkläre euch hiermit zu Mann und Frau.
I now pronounce you husband and wife.
To live in the here and now.
Die hiesigen Künstler sind sehr talentiert.
The local artists are very talented.
»Dem mag nun sein wie ihm wolle, so irren Sie doch in Ihrer ersten Voraussetzung, Mann, sintemal ich kein Volksschullehrer bin, sondern der Professor Doktor Raat vom hiesigen Gymnasium.«
"That may be as it will, but in your first condition you err, since I am no elementary school teacher, good man, but Professor Raat, Ph.D., of the local grammar school."
hiesig.et: Apparently from Middle High German *hiewesic, from Middle High German hie, hī (“here”, adverb) + Middle High German *wesic (“being”), as in Middle High German abewesic (“absent”), selpwesic (“intrinsic, essential”), etc. Equivalent to hie (“here”) + wesend + -…

s: according to this (just mentioned thing), in accordance with this
down here on earth, in this world (not up in heaven)
hienieden.et: From hie (“dated form of hier”) + nieden (“down”) (obsolete).
